repo_prior_art.cite: none; the catalogue contains no fixed-bin Hawkes two-lag inverse.

published_prior_art.cite: BacryMuzy2016 identifies from complete first/second-order functions; Koyama2025 and Kirchner2016 use coarse/small-bin approximations; ZhouPapadogeorgou2025 identifies from the full aggregated-count law.

BacryMuzy2016 retains first-order intensity alongside second-order characterization; AchabBacryGaiffasMastromatteoMuzy2017 uses second- and third-order integrated cumulants rather than this three-covariance reconstruction.
CheyssonLang2022 supplies fixed-bin Whittle consistency/asymptotic normality under full-spectrum injectivity, but not the random-image restricted-logarithm inverse.
WangXieCuozzoMakXie2020 gives rowwise exact-event-time likelihood-score confidence sets, not fixed-bin covariance-inverse graph inclusion.
BacryMuzy2016 and CheyssonLang2022 use complete covariance/spectral information; no located result classifies the stated one-lag fibers on legal labeled three-node supports.

GleserHwang1987 supplies a general unbounded-target impossibility mechanism, while WangXieCuozzoMakXie2020 and CheyssonLang2022 address regular exact-time or fixed-model settings rather than this bounded-metric Hawkes frontier.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:1401.0903v2, corresponding to IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 62 (2016)
source_verification_receipts.locator: PDF pp. 3–4, Proposition 2, Theorem 1, Equation (19), and Corollary 1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves unique causal Wiener–Hopf recovery from the complete correlation/conditional-expectation function and first-order intensity, not recovery from finitely many binned covariance lags.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2003.04314, corresponding to Annals of Statistics 50 (2022)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper derives the aliased bin-count spectrum and establishes Whittle consistency/asymptotic normality under spectral injectivity and smoothness conditions; it does not state a finite-lag inverse.

source_verification_receipts.locator: PDF pp. 1–2, abstract and introduction; Section 3/Theorem 2 as identified by the publication
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper constructs an INAR(infinity)-based family converging weakly to a Hawkes process as the bin width tends to zero, rather than an exact positive-bin inverse.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Publisher abstract and article record; Section 3.4 / Theorem 2 and Equation (18) are the supplied primary anchors
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article introduces a coarse-grained approximation framework for binned Hawkes data and parameter inference; its stated target is second-order approximation, not the proposal's exact two-covariance recovery functional.

source_verification_receipts.locator: PDF pp. 1–3 and 8–11, abstract, introduction, and aggregated-data likelihood formulation
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The work proves identifiability from aggregated-data distributions under model conditions and uses latent exact event patterns/branching structure; it does not reduce identification to three population covariance matrices.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2108.12357, corresponding to Statistics and Computing 32 (2022)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The multivariate method treats binned counts as observed and exact event times as latent data in a Monte Carlo EM procedure.

source_verification_receipts.locator: PDF pp. 2–5, Equations (2)–(5), Theorem 3.1, and Section 3.2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The method is based on continuous-time likelihood, score, history covariates, and rowwise excitation-weight inference, rather than fixed-bin covariance moments.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 2, Theorem 1, as cited in the proposal
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The cited result concerns infinite expected diameter when an unbounded parameter is lost along a nuisance limit; it motivates but does not settle the bounded-metric Hawkes adaptation problem.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a symbolic three-node diamond calculation of the restricted transition, finite logarithm, and skew-jump orientation, so the non-invertible-image mechanism is independently auditable beyond the numerical diagnostic.
State and prove a surplus-lag specification corollary using Gamma_3 onward, explicitly separating the common-decay acyclic model from heterogeneous-decay, cyclic, and nonexponential alternatives.
Develop the boundary OEQ into a matched local lower/upper frontier for at least the empty-graph and one-weak-edge submodels before attempting the full unknown-rank union.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 with the exact two-lag identification theorem as the field-tier kernel; use a three-node symbolic worked instance as the first proof checkpoint.
